question.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
question.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
question.clue: The eventual victors in this conflict collected a tribute called the paria from the ta'ifa principalities that emerged after the collapse of the Almohad Caliphate.

swap.text: This was the largest boat of the three in Columbus's fleet. It ran aground due to incompetent piloting and was dismantled to build the first Spanish settlement in the New World.
swap.clue: This ship, the largest and slowest of the three that Christopher Columbus used in his first voyage to the Americas.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Counter-Reformation.
question.text: This institution of the Counter-Reformation, whose first chief was Tomas de Torquemada, was established by Isabella I of Castile to root out Moriscos, Jews, and non-Catholics.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Inquisition [or Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition]
question.clue: Tomas de Torquemada led this organization, which used a seal that quoted Psalm 73, and frequently used the auto-da-fe to publicly burn heretics.

swap.text: The expeditions of Columbus were sponsored by this queen, who ruled Spain on equal terms alongside her husband Ferdinand.
swap.answerHtml: Queen Isabella [or Isabella I; or Isabella the Catholic; accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, Isabella of Castile]

question.text: The Sicilians offered the throne to this kingdom's Peter III (Peter the Third), which led to the pope calling for a crusade named after this kingdom.
question.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

swap.leadin: This 1494 agreement was extended by the Treaty of Zaragoza in 1529.
swap.text: Name this treaty signed by Pope Alexander VI that divided the New World between Spain and Portugal. It created a line of demarcation 100 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands.
swap.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

question.leadin: The Condor Legion provided bombing support for one side during this war, including during its Battle of the Ebro.
question.text: Name this war in which the Nationalist forces of Francisco Franco defeated the Republicans.
question.clue: The Abraham Lincoln Battalion was one of the International Brigades that fought in this conflict.

swap.leadin: The Duke of Medina Sidonia commanded this fleet.
swap.text: Name this fleet that set sail in 1588 with the aim of overthrowing Queen Elizabeth I. This fleet was blown off course by a "Protestant wind" that wrecked many of its ships in the English Channel.
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.leadin: This rival of Emilio Mola originally led the Army of Africa in revolt.
question.text: Name this leader who maintained the Plazas de soberania and signed a Pact with Eisenhower that helped start his country's economic miracle from 1959 to 1973. He was succeeded by Juan Carlos.
question.clue: In another conflict, this future leader worked with a commander who coined the phrase "fifth column" and was aided by the Condor Legion.

swap.text: The physician Abu al-Qasim did pioneering work on dissections and removing bladder stones in this city. Abd ar-Rahman III ruled from this city, whose massive Great Mosque contained a Court of the Oranges and was converted to a Catholic cathedral in 1236.
swap.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

question.text: Before the founding of the UAW, automotive workers got into a battle named after this city during a strike against Electric Auto-Lite. A war named after this city resulted from a dispute about the southern border of Michigan.
question.clue: At this city's third council, the term filioque was incorporated into the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed for the first time in Western Christianity.

swap.leadin: This group declared a ceasefire in September 2010 after an earlier, broken "permanent ceasefire" in 2006.
swap.text: Name this group responsible for assassinating Prime Minister Luis Carrero Blanco in 1973 and accused by some of carrying out some 2004 train bombings in a capital city.
swap.clue: This group's political wing was the Herri Batasuna.

question.text: Searching for the land of Bimini, this guy spent his career surveying Florida in the early 1500s supposedly in pursuit of the Fountain of Youth.
question.clue: Appointed as governor of Higuey, he had previously served as a lieutenant under Nicolas de Ovando.

swap.leadin: Ringtones featuring this person's voice became popular after he interrupted Hugo Chavez, asking him, "Why don't you shut up?"
swap.text: Name this ruler of Spain from 1975 to 2014, when he abdicated in favor of his son Felipe VI. This ruler oversaw the Spanish transition to democracy.
swap.clue: This head of state asked Hugo Chavez "Why don't you shut up?" at a meeting where Chavez repeatedly interrupted one of his countrymen.

question.leadin: In November 2014, Spanish prosecutors announced charges against Artur Mas for illegally conducting a referendum on this question.
question.text: Identify this cause which seeks to make Barcelona the capital of a new country.
question.clue: The paramilitary Terra Lliure ("LEEW-ruh") and the ERC party both support this cause, whose "refoundation" was led by Artur Mas.

swap.leadin: His reign included the updating of Arabic astronomical tables.
swap.text: Name this Spanish monarch, the tenth king of his name, who ruled from 1252 to 1284 and was known as 'el Sabio' because of his encouragement of learning.
swap.clue: It was for this king that Jehuda ben Moses Cohen and Isaac ben Sid assembled namesake astronomical tables.

question.leadin: After the fall of this king's last valido, Luis Mendez de Haro, this king relied on the mystical nun Maria de Agreda for advice on governance.
question.text: Name this "Planet King." His chief minister for the first twenty-two years of his rule was the expansionist Count-Duke of Olivares.
question.answerHtml: Philip IV of Spain [or Philip III of Portugal; prompt on Philip; do not accept or prompt on “Philip III” alone]
question.clue: He began the construction of the Buen Retiro palace, which featured the Hall of Realms, which led to this ruler's designation as the "Planet King."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about eagles in history.
swap.text: Bertrand du Guesclin, the man known as the "Eagle of Brittany" and the "Black Dog of Broceliande," was defeated in this 1367 battle in Spain. Edward the Black Prince and John of Gaunt allied with Peter the Cruel to defeat the French-backed forces of Henry of Trastamara here.
swap.clue: This 1367 clash during the Castilian Civil War, won by Pedro the Cruel thanks to English support led by a pair of brothers including John of Gaunt.

question.leadin: It was ended by the Treaty of the Hague.
question.text: Identify this conflict between Philip V of Spain and France, England, the Netherlands and Austria who felt that Spain should pony up more funds for sucking it hard during War of Spanish Succession.
question.clue: The most important military victory of this war was won by George Byng in the Battle of Cape Passaro.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about the Muslim conquest of Spain.
swap.text: This man escaped to Spain after the Abbasids had all the Ummayad princes murdered and became emir of Cordoba whereupon he ordered the construction of the Great Mosque of Cordoba.
swap.clue: After the Umayyads were defeated by the Franks, they would, under this ruler, eventually establish an emirate in Cordoba that would survive until 1031 and be distinct from the main Caliphate of Damascus. The first ruler of the later Caliphate of Cordoba also had this name.
